title: ECG
text: An electrocardiogram records the heart's electrical activity from electrodes on the skin.

children.title: Signal origin
children.text: Each heartbeat starts in the SA node and spreads through the heart, creating tiny voltage changes at the skin.

children.title: Waves
children.text: P = atrial depolarisation, QRS = ventricular depolarisation, T = ventricular repolarisation.

children.title: Intervals
children.text: PR interval, QRS width and QT interval reveal conduction delays and rhythm risks.

children.title: Leads
children.text: A standard 12-lead ECG views the heart from 12 angles using limb and chest electrodes.

children.title: Front-end
children.text: Instrumentation amplifiers, filters and ADCs boost microvolt signals and reject noise.

children.title: Filtering
children.text: Band-pass filters remove baseline wander and muscle noise; a notch filter removes mains hum.

children.title: QRS detection
children.text: Algorithms such as Pan–Tompkins find R-peaks, giving heart rate and variability.
